subject.title: Rebrand text-substitution filter on tool-call arguments silently misroutes file ops

question: What permanent boundary should plugin text transforms use for path-like and tool-bearing text: skip those contexts, make only specific transform scopes opt in, or preserve broad replacement behavior with a separate recovery/diagnostic path?
rationale: The same API currently serves cosmetic rebrand shims, privacy/entity restoration, CLI prompt shaping, and provider structured tool-call argument restoration, so an automated repair cannot safely choose the contract boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define path-safe transform scopes
options.body: Keep text transforms for prompt/display/entity restoration, but add an explicit path/tool-bearing safety rule plus tests and documentation for when replacements do not run.

options.title: Preserve broad transforms and add diagnostics
options.body: Keep current replacement semantics for compatibility, then add opt-out/debug/doctor guidance so affected users can diagnose and recover from split workspaces.

options.title: Replace with explicit plugin hooks
options.body: Deprecate broad text transforms for executable payloads and move tool/persistence rewriting into narrower hooks, accepting a larger Plugin SDK design pass.

recommendation.title: Define path-safe transform scopes
recommendation.body: Keep text transforms for prompt/display/entity restoration, but add an explicit path/tool-bearing safety rule plus tests and documentation for when replacements do not run.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the text-transform surface and is the strongest routing candidate for choosing whether the current broad behavior should remain intentional.
